title.narrative: OHCHR Asia-Pacific promote and protect human rights
OHCHR Strengthening cap. of reg. actors to protect human rights

description.narrative:
Insatsen syftar till att bidra till genomförandet av Sveriges regionala strategi för utvecklinssamarbetet i Asien och Oceanien genom att stärka OHCHR:s regionala kontor i Asien och Stilla havet. Syftet är att bidra till att stärka regionala aktörers kapacitet att främja mänskliga rättigheter, ansvarutkrävande, demokratiskt utrymme och jämställdhet i Asien och Oceanien.
Insatsen innebär ett finansiellt regionalt programstöd till FN:s Högkommissiaries regionala kontor i Bangkok och Suva. Insatsen avser att bidra till genomförandet av OHCHR's regionala program för Asien och Stilla havet och följer OHCHR strategiska plan och deras regionala program för Asien och Oceanien.
Projektet syftar framför allt till att möjligöra att OHCHR kan stärka bemanning och kapaciteten av det regionala kontoret i Bangkok genom inrättandet av 7 nya tjänster med spjutspetskomptens inom områden som miljö/klimat, ekonomiska sociala och kulturella rättigheter och migration, inklusive människohandel och migration.
I OHCHR:s projektunderlag har de föreslagit att Sverige ska bidra till följande områden:
- Stärk kapacitet hos regionala aktörer att integrera mänskliga rättigheter i arbete med migration, människohandel och modernt slaveri - Stärkt kapacitet hos regionala aktörer att främja mänskliga rättigheter i relation till klimatförändringar, miljö samt ekonomiska, sociala och kulturella rättigheter - Stärkt kapacitet hos regionala aktörer att främja och skydda det demokratiska utrymmet - Stärkta regionala mekanismer för att främja och skydda mänskliga rättigheter - Ökad integrering av mänskliga rättigheter inom FN-systemet, inklusive FN:s utvecklingsgrupp med ansvar för Asien och Stilla havet.

Program support to OHCHR regional Office. The contribution aims to strengthen the capacity of regional actors to promote human rights, accountability, democratic space and gender in Asia and the Pacific.

The intervention seeks to improve the capacity of regional and national actors to respect, protect and implement human rights in the Asia-Pacific region. The direct target groups are states in their capacity as duty-bearers and responsible for their human rights obligations and civil society organisations, academia and other actors working to strengthen the capacity of rights holders to claim their rights. OHCHR seek to increase the knowledge about international standards and state obligations for human rights and how these translate into the human rights challenges faced in the Asia-Pacific region.
The project has five result areas: i) Expected result 1 (RO1): strengthened capacity of regional actors to address human rights issues related to migration, trafficking and modern slavery. ii) Expected result 2 (RO2): strengthened capacity of regional actors to promote human rights arising in the context of climate change, including economic, social and cultural rights, and environmental rights iii) Expected result 3 (RO3): strengthened capacity of regional actors to promote and protect democratic space. iv) Expected result 4 (RO4): strengthened regional mechanisms to promote and protect human rights v) Expected result 5 (RO5): human rights mainstreaming within the UN system, including the UN development group for the Asia-Pacific

Summary of key results from the 7 year project Sweden supported during 2018-2025:
- Through OHCHR's support, important achievements in strengthening human rights protection across Asia and the Pacific have been made. A key result area has been on migration, human trafficking, and modern slavery, where OHCHR led research and advocacy enhanced legal and policy actions to protect vulnerable migrants, particularly those trapped in online scam centers in Cambodia, Myanmar, Lao PDR, and the Philippines. Through strengthened networking, legal professionals improved their capacity to advocate for migrants' rights. Regional cooperation also advanced with the adoption of the Pacific Regional Framework on Climate Mobility, which integrates strong human rights safeguards for climate induced migration. The normative role OHCHR played has also contributed to essential progress made in advocating migration rights which includes behavioral change and improved public perceptions of migrants.
- Regional bodies, including ASEAN and the Pacific Islands Forum, saw improved capacities to implement obligations related to the right to a healthy environment with technical support from OHCHR. Additionally, the private sector engaged more actively in discussions on business impact on human rights and climate change, with an emphasis on protecting marginalized communities. National action plans on Business and Human Rights have been adopted with broader civil society participation in countries OHCHR engaged and supported. Pacific nations, including Kiribati, Tuvalu and Vanuatu, integrated environmental rights into their Business and Human Rights policy frameworks. Advocacy on climate justice to amplify the voices of youth and environmental defenders was enhanced through the Asia-Pacific Environmental Human Rights Defenders Forum which OHCHR organizes every year.
- Despite the regional challenges for democracy, the protection of democratic space was reinforced through digital security initiatives targeting civil society actors, particularly women human rights defenders (WHRDs). A new digital security training package was launched, and a regional report on the impact of new technologies on civic space highlighted emerging threats. Further, civil society actors in Lao PDR and Malaysia strengthened their engagement with UN human rights mechanisms, leading to increased legal actions and international scrutiny of human rights violations.
- Regional human rights mechanisms have been strengthened, including enhanced knowledge and role of the ASEAN Intergovernmental Commission on Human Rights (AICHR). These efforts helped pave the way for ongoing work on the ASEAN Environmental Rights Framework, advancing environmental justice in Southeast Asia.
